FR-001.title: The Overseer MUST be able to create, rename, and dissolve terminal groups and to move terminals between groups within the current session.

FR-002.title: Each terminal MUST belong to exactly one terminal group at all times.

FR-003.title: A terminal that is not coupled with another terminal MUST be represented by a singleton group containing only that terminal.
tests: tests/browser/terminal-grouping.spec.mjs::splits one terminal into a collision-safe singleton only after confirmation

FR-004.title: Each terminal group MUST have a stable identity and a non-empty display name unique within the session after trimming and case normalization.

FR-005.title: Saved sessions MUST preserve terminal groups and each terminal's membership across close and reopen.

FR-006.title: Dissolving or merging a group MUST preserve every terminal and its content while leaving no zero-member group after the operation.

FR-007.title: The transition destination editor MUST offer only other terminals that currently share the source terminal's group.

FR-008.title: A forward terminal transition MUST be eligible only when its source and destination exist and currently belong to the same non-empty group.

FR-009.title: Selecting an eligible forward transition MUST create exactly one pending Overseer decision without changing the active terminal or route.

FR-010.title: Approving a forward transition MUST revalidate the authored link, both terminals, and their shared group before changing the active terminal.

FR-011.title: Rejecting or closing a forward transition decision MUST leave the active terminal and route unchanged.

FR-012.title: An approved forward transition MUST add exactly one return point for its source terminal.

FR-013.title: A backward terminal return MUST be eligible only when the active terminal and saved return terminal currently belong to the same non-empty group.

FR-014.title: Selecting an eligible backward return MUST create exactly one pending Overseer decision without changing the active terminal or route.

FR-015.title: Approving a backward return MUST revalidate the current route point and shared group before changing the active terminal.

FR-016.title: An approved backward return MUST remove exactly the most recent route point.

FR-017.title: Rejecting or closing a backward return decision MUST leave the active terminal and route unchanged.

FR-018.title: The system MUST reject any authored or submitted transition whose endpoints are cross-group, missing from group representation, missing as terminals, or identical.
tests: tests/browser/terminal-grouping.spec.mjs::rejects a group proposal that would split an authored transition

FR-019.title: The system MUST reject a group edit that would leave an authored terminal-transition command crossing a group boundary.

FR-020.title: The system MUST reject a group edit that would invalidate a pending transition or an active return-route pair.

FR-021.title: A rejected group edit MUST identify the affected terminal or transition without partially applying the edit.
tests: tests/browser/terminal-grouping.spec.mjs::rejects a group proposal that would split an authored transition

FR-022.title: Group creation, membership changes, and group removal MUST be available only to the Overseer.

FR-023.title: Sessions created before terminal grouping MUST open with their existing terminal content intact and with one singleton group representing each terminal.

FR-024.title: Existing transition commands in an older session MUST remain authored but MUST NOT execute until both endpoints are intentionally coupled into one group.

FR-025.title: Direct Overseer terminal activation MAY cross group boundaries and MUST retain its existing route-clearing behavior.
tests: tests/browser/terminal-grouping.spec.mjs::cross-group direct Overseer activation clears the player-created return route

FR-026.title: Existing approval behavior for ordinary and state-changing commands MUST remain unchanged.

FR-027.title: Connected player views MUST converge on the same authoritative terminal-navigation state after each accepted same-group transition or return.

FR-028.title: Group or terminal changes made while a decision is pending MUST be revalidated at approval time before any transition effect occurs.

FR-029.title: Each terminal group MUST preserve one explicit, deterministic order for all of its member terminals.

FR-030.title: Starting a fresh broadcast with any grouped terminal as its first active terminal MUST establish that terminal's position in the full ordered group without discarding members before or after it.

FR-031.title: When a fresh broadcast starts from a non-first group member, backward navigation MUST make each preceding member reachable in reverse group order even though those terminals were not visited earlier in the broadcast.

FR-032.title: Starting a fresh broadcast from a non-first group member MUST NOT prevent approved forward navigation from reaching every following member or from later traversing from the group's first member through the full ordered group.

FR-033.title: Every forward or backward transition created from the initialized group position MUST require exactly one Overseer approval before changing the active terminal or navigation position.

FR-034.title: The system MUST reject a group reorder that would invalidate the current initialized position, a pending transition, or an active route without partially applying the reorder.

FR-035.title: Terminal groups MUST be the highest-level terminal representation, with terminals presented as members beneath groups rather than as ungrouped top-level items.

FR-036.title: Every persisted terminal group MUST contain at least one terminal.

FR-037.title: Creating or importing a standalone terminal MUST atomically create a singleton group that represents it.

FR-038.title: Moving or deleting the last member of a group MUST atomically remove the empty source group while keeping every surviving terminal represented by exactly one group.

FR-039.title: Creating a group by reassigning existing terminals, dissolving or merging groups, splitting members, moving terminals, or changing traversal order MUST require explicit Overseer confirmation before any state changes.
tests: tests/browser/terminal-grouping.spec.mjs::splits one terminal into a collision-safe singleton only after confirmation

FR-040.title: A destructive group-change confirmation MUST identify the proposed action, every affected group and terminal, and the resulting membership or traversal-order impact.
tests: tests/browser/terminal-grouping.spec.mjs::classifies and repairs the exact authored cold-storage document
tests/browser/desktop-api.spec.mjs::multi-link legacy partial and complete candidates remain exact at the desktop facade

FR-041.title: Cancelling, closing, or dismissing a destructive group-change confirmation MUST leave durable group data and current navigation state unchanged.

FR-042.title: Confirming a destructive group change MUST revalidate the current groups, authored links, pending decisions, active terminal, and active route before applying the proposal.
tests: tests/browser/terminal-grouping.spec.mjs::classifies and repairs the exact authored cold-storage document

FR-043.title: A confirmed destructive group change MUST either apply exactly once as one complete change or be rejected without partial effects.
tests: internal/session/service_test.go::exact authored cold storage group replacement
app_test.go::exact authored cold storage group replacement

FR-044.title: A repeated or stale destructive confirmation MUST produce no additional group or navigation change and MUST explain that the proposal is no longer applicable.

FR-045.title: A rename-only change MUST preserve the group's stable identity, membership order, authored links, pending decisions, and active route.

FR-046.title: Dissolving a multi-terminal group MUST preserve its terminals by representing each remaining member through a singleton group unless the same confirmed operation moves that member to another group.

FR-047.title: Dissolving a singleton group without moving or deleting its terminal in the same operation MUST be unavailable or rejected.

FR-052.title: Legacy repair candidate is evaluated against complete resultant membership.

intent: Give the Overseer safe create, rename, dissolve, and terminal-move controls over exact-one groups while keeping approved player navigation inside each ordered group.
expectations: Do not auto-create groups from existing links.
Do not auto-delete or retarget transition commands during regrouping.
Do not expose group management to players.
Do not restrict direct Overseer terminal activation by group.
Do not provide multi-step undo or historical restore for confirmed group changes.
approach: Represent every terminal through one durable ordered group, normalizing legacy and lifecycle changes into singleton groups. Apply group CRUD through one private whole-set compare-and-replace guarded by session and coordination revisions after structured destructive confirmation, while reusing existing approved player navigation and seeded backward routes.

decisions.decision: Store groups as session-level ordered TerminalGroup records
decisions.why: This preserves empty groups and gives membership and order one durable source of truth.
decisions.rejected: Per-terminal groupId/order fields and inference from transition links.

decisions.decision: Allow legacy no-group sessions but apply strict validation to every authored group mutation
decisions.why: Existing transition content remains readable while newly authored groups cannot leave dormant cross-group links.
decisions.rejected: Reject legacy links or permit partially grouped authored graphs.

decisions.decision: Route group changes through one coordinator-guarded control-to-session mutation
decisions.why: It serializes group edits with player navigation and closes stale generic-save bypasses.
decisions.rejected: Validate then autosave, reverse session-to-control callbacks, or freeze all broadcasts.

decisions.decision: Seed preceding ordered members as the fresh broadcast's initial LIFO backward prefix
decisions.why: The existing Back action, approval lifecycle, route projection, and reconnect behavior can cover middle starts.
decisions.rejected: A new previous/next public RPC or an empty route at a middle start.

decisions.decision: Attach runtime-only group provenance to seeded return points
decisions.why: Seeded order can be revalidated without misclassifying arbitrary authored jumps.
decisions.rejected: Infer provenance from blank command IDs or reject every reorder during a broadcast.

decisions.decision: Keep the public player schema unchanged
decisions.why: Existing route depth, return target, pending direction, and revision fields already express the required authoritative behavior.
decisions.rejected: Publish private group metadata or add a second navigation protocol.

decisions.decision: Explicitly group the checked-in demo and test legacy compatibility separately
decisions.why: The documented demo transition remains usable without auto-migrating user sessions.
decisions.rejected: Leave the demo intentionally dormant or auto-group every opened session.

decisions.decision: Treat group deletion as dissolution without terminal-content deletion
decisions.why: Every surviving terminal must remain represented by exactly one group; dissolved members become singleton groups unless atomically moved elsewhere.
decisions.rejected: Delete member terminals with the group or leave them ungrouped.

decisions.decision: Require single-use impact confirmation for membership and traversal-order changes
decisions.why: These changes can alter navigation eligibility or sequence; cancellation and stale confirmation must have zero effect.
decisions.rejected: Confirm only group deletion or apply membership changes immediately.

decisions.decision: Supersede empty-group and ungrouped compatibility designs with exact-one membership and singleton normalization
decisions.why: Groups are the mandatory high-level representation; legacy absence becomes deterministic singleton groups in memory without rewriting on open.
decisions.rejected: Persist empty groups or carry a permanent ungrouped runtime mode.

decisions.decision: Dissolve a group without deleting terminal content
decisions.why: Unassigned former members become singleton groups unless the same confirmed candidate moves them elsewhere.
decisions.rejected: Cascade-delete terminals, retain an empty group, or invent a destination group.

decisions.decision: Use a structured UI impact dialog followed by one two-revision whole-set mutation
decisions.why: Session and coordination expectations make stale, retried, and double-submitted destructive proposals zero-effect while keeping commit atomic.
decisions.rejected: Client-only validation, a separate preview-token state machine, or partial per-operation persistence.

decisions.decision: Normalize terminal create and delete within generic saves while preserving canonical memberships for existing terminals
decisions.why: Terminal lifecycle keeps exact-one representation without allowing stale full-session payloads to bypass group management.
decisions.rejected: Require a follow-up group operation or trust all groups supplied by generic autosave.

decisions.decision: Compare generic-save transition identities with the canonical document before allowing a cross-group link
decisions.why: Unchanged legacy links stay dormant while new or retargeted cross-group links are rejected
decisions.rejected: Reject every legacy cross-group save or allow all generic-save links

decisions.decision: Use a typed session-store rejection to carry only sanitized feedback and canonical revision state through coordination
decisions.why: Candidate errors remain actionable without exposing arbitrary persistence errors
decisions.rejected: Collapse every failure to a generic error or pass all store errors through

decisions.decision: Record the initial terminal identity, group, and position as runtime-only broadcast provenance
decisions.why: Group edits can validate the complete seeded successor chain and pending-return adjacency
decisions.rejected: Infer the initialized position only from the remaining route stack

decisions.decision: Derive dissolution impact from the exact generated singleton candidates
decisions.why: The confirmation names collision-adjusted groups and terminal-to-group outcomes exactly
decisions.rejected: Show only the removed group and terminal names

decisions.decision: Validate the current active terminal against the top remaining seeded return point when that route top is initial-prefix provenance
decisions.why: This mirrors approval-time seeded adjacency and rejects a reorder before it can disable the next Back action
decisions.rejected: Infer validity only from the original terminal position and stored seed-point positions

decisions.decision: Validate every seeded return point against the route point or active terminal that will eventually expose it
decisions.why: Mixed authored and seeded routes can preserve the current return while breaking a deeper future return
decisions.rejected: Checking only the current top seeded return target

decisions.decision: Expose split-to-singleton as a reviewed move destination and submit one complete replacement candidate
decisions.why: This reuses the established destructive impact and two-revision confirmation boundary
decisions.rejected: Locally mutating memberships before confirmation

decisions.decision: Identify rejected authored transitions by stable command node ID together with source and target terminal IDs
decisions.why: Endpoint pairs alone cannot distinguish multiple authored links
decisions.rejected: Index-based tree paths or command display names

decisions.decision: Collect every invalidated authored transition in canonical terminal and content-tree traversal order and join the sanitized diagnostics.
decisions.why: The existing authoring order is stable, deterministic, and preserves all command identities without inventing a secondary sort.
decisions.rejected: Return only the first conflict or sort conflicts independently of canonical authoring order.

decisions.decision: Exercise SC-001 with exactly three nontrivially ordered groups and ten explicitly asserted terminals.
decisions.why: Exact fixture and projection equality proves identities, names, group order, member order, and exact-one membership survive save/reopen.
decisions.rejected: Rely on the smaller existing two-group persistence fixture.

decisions.decision: Keep current production candidate pipeline unchanged because domain, private route, coordinator, session persistence, and reopen regressions all preserve the reviewed legacy repair candidate.
decisions.why: The only failing controlled boundary was the browser fixture navigation catalog, which retained the pre-move session after persistence; refreshing it from the accepted canonical session restores production-equivalent behavior.
decisions.rejected: Adding a production special case or weakening strict cross-group transition validation.

decisions.decision: Use an auditable implement/bugfix-BUG-002 substep to reopen a completed feature only when a patched bug report owns pending tasks.
decisions.why: This preserves prior history while allowing the normal task append/materialize and mark-complete paths to reconcile late bugfix work.
decisions.rejected: Manual lifecycle JSON or checkbox edits.

decisions.decision: Treat the reported adm-emergency rejection as an independently unresolved adjacent edge and require one complete three-terminal candidate for this authored chain.
decisions.why: The reported singleton ID for t-krel-admin is the service singleton, proving candidate membership was already in use.

decisions.decision: Treat the stale installed Desktop bundle as the first reproduced divergence and require the owned rebuilt bundle for BUG-004 acceptance.
decisions.why: The installed executable predates terminal grouping and cannot construct or submit the reviewed candidate; the rebuilt bundle preserves the exact authored candidate end to end.
decisions.rejected: Inferring candidate corruption from an error emitted without captured build identity.

decisions.decision: Show the complete resultant terminal membership in every grouping impact review.
decisions.why: A partial move must visibly leave the independently split endpoint while a complete repair must show all three endpoints before submission.
decisions.rejected: Showing only operation-local affected terminals, which can be mistaken for the final group topology.

decisions.decision: Keep strict authored-transition rejection and recover through an explicit editable all-endpoint amendment.
decisions.why: The captured candidate is intentionally partial and remains exact through every boundary; automatically committing inferred groups would violate atomic review semantics.
decisions.rejected: Weakening validation or silently auto-grouping linked terminals.
